references.text: Dibon is mentioned as a city captured by Israel in the battle against the Amorites, which explains why Gad's tribe later rebuilt it.
Dibon and Ataroth are listed among the cities that the tribes of Gad and Reuben wanted to inherit on the east side of the Jordan.
Aroer is mentioned as a city by the Arnon Valley that Israel captured from Sihon, king of the Amorites.
Dibon and Aroer are noted as part of the territory belonging to the tribe of Reuben, near the border with Gad's tribe.
Dibon is mentioned as part of the inheritance of the tribe of Reuben in Joshua's division of the land.
Dibon is mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy against Moab, reflecting the city's later history and significance.
Dibon is mentioned in Jeremiah's prophecy against Moab, indicating that the city later came under Moabite control.
Dibon is again mentioned in Jeremiah's words of judgment against Moab.
